questions.q: What does ERC in KiCad catch?
options: Trace clearance violations on the board
Wrong layers in the output Gerber and drill files
Schematic connection errors: floating pins, conflicting outputs
questions.explain: ERC checks the schematic; the fab's rules on the board are checked by DRC.

questions.q: A shunt for an INA226 at 100 A, range ±81.92 mV. Which resistance fits?
questions.explain: R ≤ 81.92 mV / 100 A ≈ 0.82 mΩ; 0.5 mΩ gives 50 mV with margin.

questions.q: How much heat does a 0.5 mΩ shunt dissipate at 40 A?
Why a Kelvin connection for the shunt?
options: To protect the board from reversed battery polarity
So the copper drop stays out of the reading
It is required by the I²C protocol
questions.explain: The sense pair leaves from the shunt pads, not from the power trace.

questions.q: External 1 oz trace width for 5 A at +10 °C per IPC-2221?
questions.explain: From I = k·ΔT^0.44·A^0.725 for 35 µm copper ≈ 2.8 mm.

questions.q: Why is a slot in the ground zone under a trace bad?
options: It noticeably increases the manufacturing cost
DRC will not pass such a board
The return current goes around the slot, and the loop radiates
No components can be placed on it
questions.explain: The current returns under the trace; going around the slot makes a large loop, an antenna.

questions.q: Where does the input capacitor of a buck converter go?
options: At the battery connector on the edge of the board
questions.explain: The loop with the fast current must be minimal.

questions.q: What do you check before first powering up an assembled board?
options: Only the look of the solder joints
Connect the battery straight away to check the current in operation
Shorts, and power from a current-limited supply
questions.explain: A continuity check and a current-limited bench supply save both the board and the battery.
